nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: POST /enquiry. Answers via Respond nodes: 400 bad email, 202 received (+ id) once saved, 200 duplicate

nodes.name: normalise
nodes.notes: Any channel -> ONE canonical envelope. Everything downstream reads only this shape

nodes.name: facts
nodes.notes: The fact table. The reply may assert NOTHING outside this. Mirror of kb/facts.yaml

nodes.name: build classify request
nodes.notes: Builds the Bedrock Converse payload. Schema + instructions live here. Forced tool call = structured JSON

nodes.notes: Bedrock Converse. Model = `config` classify_model. Synthetic data only

nodes.name: parse classification
nodes.notes: Reads the tool call + tokens; cost from `config` prices. On PARSE FAILED, the summary shows stopReason + response keys

nodes.notes: Only this category's facts. Smaller prompt, cheaper, and 'grounded on' means something

nodes.notes: Converse payload with forced tool write_reply: the reply AND the second gate (answerable?) come back together

parameters.jsCode:
// Every branch arrives here: escalate (no draft), escalate-at-gate-2 / blocked (draft kept, blocked),
// clarify and auto_send (validated draft).
return $input.all().map(item => {
  const p = item.json;
  const c = p.classification;
  const classifyCost = p.classify_cost_usd ?? 0;
  const draftCost = p.draft_cost_usd ?? 0;
  const verifyCost = p.verify_cost_usd ?? 0;

  return { json: {
    id: p.id,
    source: p.source,
    gmail_message_id: p.gmail_message_id ?? null,  // email channel only: `thread check` verifies them before a threaded draft
    gmail_thread_id: p.gmail_thread_id ?? null,
    external_key: p.external_key,
    received_at: p.received_at,
    from_email: p.from_email,
    facts_version: $('facts').first().json.facts_version ?? null,   // which fact_set version answered this enquiry (read from `facts`, like every node that uses the facts)
    is_test: p.is_test === true,                // scoring traffic (database-defined): no alert, no Gmail draft
    subject: p.subject,
    body: p.body,
    category: c.category,
    confidence: c.confidence,
    language: c.language,
    safety_flags: JSON.stringify(c.safety_flags ?? []),
    missing_slots: JSON.stringify(c.missing_slots ?? []),
    action: p.action,
    draft_reply: p.draft_reply ?? '',
    draft_stage: p.draft_stage ?? '',           // 'draft' | 'clarify' | '' (no model call)
    answerable: p.answerable ?? null,
    unanswered: p.unanswered ?? '',
    validated: p.validated === true,
    reply_blocked: p.reply_blocked === true,
    block_reason: p.block_reason ?? '',
    grounded_on: JSON.stringify(Object.keys(p.selected_facts ?? {})),
    draft_tokens: p.draft_tokens ?? null,
    classify_model: p.classify_model,
    draft_model: p.draft_model ?? null,
    verify_model: p.verify_model ?? null,
    classify_cost_usd: classifyCost,
    draft_cost_usd: draftCost,
    verify_cost_usd: verifyCost,
    total_cost_usd: Number((classifyCost + draftCost + verifyCost).toFixed(6))
  }};
});

nodes.name: prepare row
nodes.notes: All three branches land here. Flatten to one DB row; cost = classify + draft (if any)

parameters.content:
## Enquiry Desk — what this does

A customer enquiry arrives. It is **classified**, answered **only from a fact table it cannot
deviate from**, and recorded — with cost tracked per enquiry.

**The business problem.** Meridian Tutors (fictional) is staffed from the UK, 09:00–18:00 UTC.
Its customers are in Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia — UTC+8. Those UK hours are 17:00–02:00
local, so **the entire Asian business day is unstaffed.** A parent asking a question at 10am
local waits seven hours, while emailing two competitors.

**The flow**

`form → envelope → save (202) → classify → derive slots → route → draft / clarify → answerable? → verify → validate → record → review` · failures → `01 Enquiry Desk - errors`

**The design decision worth defending:** grounding comes from a **structured fact table, not RAG**.
It is auditable, cheaper, and it cannot invent a price. A tutoring company can survive a slow
reply; it cannot survive quoting a discount that does not exist.

**Cost:** ~$0.0023 per enquiry on Amazon Nova 2 Lite (Bedrock), at AWS's real per-token prices.
A model per stage and the price table live in the `config` node. Measured over 24 test cases, not estimated.

⚠️ **Sessions 1–4 done** — see the red note for what is still missing.

### ① INTAKE → ENVELOPE
Normalise first, then **write first**: the enquiry is in Postgres before any model call, so a failure can't lose it. 400 for bad input, 200 for duplicates, 202 + id once saved.

### ② UNDERSTAND → ROUTE
Cheap model, strict schema (forced tool). It **extracts** category, details and safety flags; code **decides** what's missing (`derive missing slots`) and where it goes (`route`: flag → sensitive → vague → missing → auto_send). Confidence is recorded, never routed on.

### ③ WRITE & CHECK
**auto_send:** only this category's facts → draft → *answerable?* → a second model **verifies** every claim → code **validates** numbers + availability. **clarify:** code picks the one question, the model phrases it. **escalate:** no AI draft — a human writes it.

### ④ RECORD
`record results`, one transaction: enquiry (status → processed), `run_log` (cost + model per stage), `reply` (blocked ones with the reason). Nothing is sent. By design.

## ⚠️ Not finished — nothing is sent yet

- **In:** write-first intake, routing, the second gate, one-question clarify, a claim validator, a **failure path** (any production failure marks the row `failed` (dead letter), logs it and sends a Telegram alert; `test/replay.py` re-runs failed enquiries) and **human review**: escalated and blocked enquiries send a Telegram "needs review" link (no customer data) to a private review page where a person approves the draft or takes over.
- **Measured:** 24 labelled cases, `test/score.py`: category 22/24, safety flags 6/6, 0 invented claims reach a reply. t06's £190 bundle is **blocked**.
- **Claims:** numbers by regex, availability by code, every other factual statement by a **second model** (`verify`) that must quote its evidence. It caught a real error: a draft putting GCSE Maths on Saturdays. Residual risk: the verifier is a model.
- **Nothing is sent.** Approved replies are stored with `approved_at`; `sent_at` stays empty.

**Next:** a real outbound channel (an approved reply becomes a draft in the business inbox).

nodes.name: config
nodes.notes: One model per stage (classify / draft / verify / clarify) and a price table in $ per million tokens. Change a stage's model = edit its *_model here; its price comes from model_prices

nodes.name: derive missing slots
nodes.notes: Model says what the customer SAID; this rule table decides what's MISSING. Testable, no model judgement

nodes.name: route
nodes.notes: First match wins. Flags above everything: a flag at 0.99 confidence still escalates. Confidence is NOT used

nodes.name: action = escalate
nodes.notes: No AI draft: a human writes this one

nodes.name: action = clarify
nodes.notes: Missing details or too vague -> a one-question reply (code picks what to ask)

nodes.name: action = auto_send
nodes.notes: Provisional: the second gate (can <facts> answer it?) can still escalate. Nothing is sent yet

nodes.name: read draft
nodes.notes: Reads write_reply {reply, answerable, unanswered}. No tool call = not answerable (a human looks)

nodes.name: answerable?
nodes.notes: Second gate. False = the facts can't answer it, or a person must act -> escalate

nodes.name: action = escalate (gate 2)
nodes.notes: Draft kept for the human, stored as blocked with the reason

nodes.name: build clarify request
nodes.notes: WHAT to ask comes from code (missing_slots). The model only phrases it, in their language

nodes.name: clarify
nodes.notes: Amazon Nova 2 Lite on Bedrock (Converse). One-question reply. Synthetic data only

nodes.name: read clarify
nodes.notes: Exactly one question, checked in code. Otherwise a fixed template is used

nodes.name: validate claims
nodes.notes: Numbers by regex, availability by code, free-text claims by the verifier. Any problem -> blocked

parameters.query:
insert into enquiry (id, source, external_key, received_at, from_email, subject, body, status, n8n_execution_id, gmail_message_id, gmail_thread_id)
values ($1::uuid, $2, $3, $4::timestamptz, $5, $6, $7, 'received', $8, nullif($9, ''), nullif($10, ''))
on conflict (external_key) do update
  set status = 'received',
      n8n_execution_id = excluded.n8n_execution_id,
      received_at = excluded.received_at
  where enquiry.status = 'failed'      -- only a FAILED row can be reclaimed (replay); anything else is a duplicate
returning id, is_test;

nodes.name: record received
nodes.notes: WRITE FIRST: the enquiry is safe in Postgres before any model call. Duplicate = 0 rows = run stops (free). A failed row can be reclaimed by a replay

nodes.name: envelope
nodes.notes: Puts the envelope back with the row's real id, and flags duplicates (no id returned)

nodes.name: valid email?
nodes.notes: Bad input gets a 400 straight back - it is not a failure, so no dead letter and no alert

nodes.name: respond 400
nodes.notes: Tells the sender what's wrong. Nothing stored

nodes.name: duplicate?
nodes.notes: Same email + message today, already handled -> say so and stop (no model calls)

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, status: 'duplicate', message: 'We already have this enquiry.' }) }}

nodes.name: respond duplicate
nodes.notes: 200: we already have it. The run ends here

nodes.name: respond 202
nodes.notes: 202 + reference id, sent only once the enquiry is safely in Postgres. Processing continues after

nodes.name: build verify request
nodes.notes: Claim check: a SECOND model lists every factual statement and whether <facts> support it

nodes.name: verify
nodes.notes: Amazon Nova 2 Lite on Bedrock (Converse). Claim check, temperature 0. Synthetic data only

nodes.name: read verify
nodes.notes: Any claim not supported === true -> a claim problem (no result = problem: a human looks)

nodes.name: needs review?
nodes.notes: escalate or blocked -> a person reviews it. auto_send and clarify don't

parameters.query:
update enquiry
   set review_status = 'pending', review_token = replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', ''), reviewed_at = null
 where id = $1::uuid
returning id, review_token;

nodes.name: open review
nodes.notes: review_status = pending + a random review_token (the link's key)

parameters.text: ={{ '🔎 Enquiry needs review\nCategory: ' + $('prepare row').first().json.category + ' · action: ' + $('prepare row').first().json.action + '\n' + ($('prepare row').first().json.draft_reply ? 'A draft is ready — approve it or take over.' : 'No AI draft — a person writes this one.') }}

nodes.name: review alert
nodes.notes: Category + action + Open review link. NO customer data in Telegram. Link works on the tailnet only

nodes.name: notify a human?
nodes.notes: scoring traffic (enquiry.is_test) still gets a review, but no Telegram message - the test suite must not page anyone

nodes.name: to record
nodes.notes: Join point: every branch meets here, one line into ④. Passes items through unchanged

nodes.name: draft for cleared?
nodes.notes: Cleared (auto_send) and clarify replies get a Gmail DRAFT too. Not blocked, has text, and not scoring traffic (enquiry.is_test) so test runs don't fill the mailbox

nodes.name: create gmail draft
nodes.notes: DRAFT only, addressed to the customer. Nothing is ever sent: a person presses Send in Gmail. If Gmail fails the enquiry is unaffected (see record draft)

parameters.query:
update reply
   set drafted_at = case when $2::text <> '' then now() end,
       gmail_draft_id = nullif($2::text, ''),
       draft_error = nullif($3::text, '')
 where enquiry_id = $1::uuid and body <> ''
returning enquiry_id as id, gmail_draft_id, draft_error;

nodes.name: record draft
nodes.notes: Records the Gmail draft id, or why there is none. sent_at is never set here

nodes.name: load facts

parameters.query: select version, doc from fact_set where status = 'live' order by version desc limit 1;

nodes.notes: The fact table lives in the database (fact_set), versioned. This reads the one live version; the staging workflow reads the staging database's, production reads production's. No live row = Always Output Data still passes an empty item, so the next node runs and throws, the run fails loudly and the errors workflow takes over (the enquiry is already saved)

nodes.name: from email?
nodes.notes: Came in by email with a Gmail message id? Then check the thread before drafting into it

nodes.name: get original
nodes.notes: Read the customer's message from Gmail itself (the webhook's ids are only hints)

nodes.name: thread check
nodes.notes: Thread only if Gmail says this sender wrote that message; otherwise a fresh draft

parameters.query:
-- One statement, so the three writes succeed or fail together (no half-recorded enquiry).
with upd as (
  update enquiry
     set category = $2, confidence = $3::numeric, language = $4,
         safety_flags = $5::jsonb, missing_slots = $6::jsonb, action = $7,
         facts_version = $8::int,
         status = 'processed'
   where id = $1::uuid
  returning id
), log as (
  -- classify always; draft/clarify when a reply was written; verify when it ran; validate (ok/failed + reason) when checked
  insert into run_log (enquiry_id, stage, status, attempt, model, cost_usd, error)
  select $1::uuid, 'classify', 'ok', 1, $9::text, $10::numeric, null::text
  union all
  select $1::uuid, $12::text, 'ok', 1, $17::text, $11::numeric, null::text where $12::text <> ''
  union all
  select $1::uuid, 'verify', 'ok', 1, $18::text, $16::numeric, null::text where $16::numeric > 0
  union all
  select $1::uuid, 'validate', case when $13::boolean then 'failed' else 'ok' end, 1, null::text,
         0::numeric, nullif($14::text, '') where $15::boolean
), rep as (
  -- every written reply, blocked or not, with the reason; sent_at stays null
  insert into reply (id, enquiry_id, body, grounded_on, blocked, block_reason)
  select gen_random_uuid(), $1::uuid, $19::text, $20::jsonb, $13::boolean, nullif($14::text, '')
  where coalesce($19::text, '') <> ''
)
select id from upd;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('prepare row').first().json.id, $('prepare row').first().json.category, $('prepare row').first().json.confidence, $('prepare row').first().json.language, $('prepare row').first().json.safety_flags, $('prepare row').first().json.missing_slots, $('prepare row').first().json.action, $('prepare row').first().json.facts_version, $('prepare row').first().json.classify_model, $('prepare row').first().json.classify_cost_usd, $('prepare row').first().json.draft_cost_usd, $('prepare row').first().json.draft_stage, $('prepare row').first().json.reply_blocked, $('prepare row').first().json.block_reason, $('prepare row').first().json.validated, $('prepare row').first().json.verify_cost_usd, $('prepare row').first().json.draft_model, $('prepare row').first().json.verify_model, $('prepare row').first().json.draft_reply, $('prepare row').first().json.grounded_on ] }}

nodes.name: record results
nodes.notes: One transaction: enquiry → processed, run_log (cost + model per stage), reply (if one was written). Nothing is sent
